why: This is the heap's own construction routine: treat the array as a complete binary tree and run Floyd's bottom-up heapify, sifting each internal node down from the last parent to the root. The tie rules only pin down which of several valid heaps you must output.
hints: Leaves (indices n//2 and beyond) are already one-element heaps. Which nodes actually need work, and in what order?
Go from index n//2 - 1 down to 0. Sift each node down: compare it with its larger child (left wins ties) and swap only if that child is strictly greater, then keep going from the child's position.
In-place sift-down on the array; bottom-up heapify costs O(n) total (most nodes are near the bottom and sift only a little), O(1) extra space.
pitfalls: Pick the right child only when it is strictly greater than the left; equal children go left.
Swap only when the child is strictly greater than the parent; equal values stay put.
Empty input and a single element return as is.
Inserting elements one by one (top-down) gives a different valid heap; the expected answer needs bottom-up order.
